H: After a logical key is admitted under one keysym-to-keycode mapping, changing that mapping before explicit key-up must not leave the originally admitted physical key down. The admission and explicit-up receipts must identify the same physical keycode.
T: One fake-Xlib case: admit W as keycode 87, remap W to 77, request up for W, then inspect physical fake key state and owner receipts.

D.baseline: FAIL only if code 87 remains down and no explicit-up receipt identifies it.
D.candidate: PASS only if physical state is empty and admission.keycode equals owner_explicit_keyup.keycode equals 87, with request-start <= XSync-return.

C: A changed mapping may change the symbol interpretation, but an up paired with a currently held logical key must release the physical code admitted for that hold; typed keymap-epoch checks remain necessary for semantic interpretation.
U: Fake Xlib/source-composition only. This does not establish real X server remap delivery, physical transition time, GUI/game effect, model behavior, bounded recovery, or live threat response.
runtime: python3 fake Xlib on macOS host; no game or X server
